emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Proposed bounded applicant-support workflow: retrieve approved program information, ask clarifying questions, plan next steps, and request a counselor appointment through a permission-limited tool. Staff approve outbound messages and any record changes. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
organization: NYU School of Professional Studies (SPS) - graduate admissions
industry_sector: Higher education - graduate and professional admissions and recruitment. Applicant trust, privacy, accessibility and accuracy matter; international applicants include EU residents; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Reduce repetitive inquiry handling and improve timely guidance through the staged path the Adoption specialist permits for this application class: a proof of concept now, then a gated bounded experiment (C4). Actual demand, response time and benefits have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students; admissions counselors (would review and approve agent drafts); SPS enrollment management leadership (sponsor of this evaluation); marketing/enrollment staff (maintain program content); NYU IT and SPS technology staff; NYU privacy and compliance officers
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast-follower (held constant across the primary and both contrasts; for NYU SPS this is a course-case assumption, not an official policy).
capabilities_constraints: Verified: SPS offers a public chatbot named Violet (D18); NYU Admissions runs a generative-AI admissions bot with hand-off to a live agent (D17); NYU IT offers Gemini, NotebookLM, Microsoft Copilot and a private GenAI service (D31); NYU's Electronic Data and System Risk Classification Policy applies (D32). Course-case assumptions (not verified NYU facts): SPS enrollment management leadership asked for this evaluation and has funded only the proof of concept; admissions counselors would review agent drafts on top of current duties, with no backfill planned; program content is maintained by marketing/enrollment staff, and who owns Violet's content and incidents is not documented in the supplied information; CRM and scheduling integration and the vendor are not selected or verified; no AI-specific privacy/compliance review of an applicant-facing agent has started. Not supplied: weekly and peak-season web-inquiry volume, counselor hours that could be protected for review, target response time, and staff views of the change.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong deadlines or promises can harm applicants, and the organization is accountable for what its agent says (D21); unauthorized actions can expose data. No applicant records are used in this assignment. No legal determination is made.
management_question: Is NYU SPS ready to implement and sustain this application along the permitted path (proof of concept, then a gated bounded experiment), what is the most consequential readiness gap, and what must change before management proceeds?
time_horizon: 12 months: proof of concept this term; bounded-experiment decision within this admissions cycle
additional_context: Upstream: the Adoption specialist (C4) classifies agent-based applicant support as bleeding edge and permits a proof of concept now, gated (G1-G4) to a bounded experiment (at most 10% of web inquiries, 8 weeks, staff approve every message, no record writes, stop rule); G3 is compliance sign-off and G4 is confirmed approval capacity. A3-A5 (C3): compare staff-only, simple retrieval and the agent first; significance carries Low weight; denominator rule. Use the dated source register. Primary case.
